outcome.definition: Subsequent APTT was therapeutic at the specified follow-up time

canonical_statement: Success rates were calculated as therapeutic APTT results divided by total APTT determinations at the specified follow-up time, and study-control success rates were compared with a chi-square statistic.

The initial nomogram was pretested in 20 patients from July through November 1988, modified after those results, tested in 10 additional patients, and refined before the final nomogram became available January 1, 1989.

canonical_statement: The authors identified potential patient-selection bias from comparison with historical controls.
The study sample was too small to support a valid comparison of recurrent venous thromboembolism or bleeding outcomes between groups.

The final nomogram was developed for the Actin FS thromboplastin reagent and the authors stated that it was unlikely to be generalizable to other APTT reagents without local comparison or heparin-assay calibration.
The authors reported wide institutional acceptance of the nomogram among hematologists, internists, and ward nurses.
The authors concluded that the nomogram standardized heparin therapy and enabled more rapid achievement and maintenance of therapeutic APTT values while reducing time outside the therapeutic range.
The study was supported in part by the Heart and Stroke Foundation of Ontario.
